p.src: It was not yet the second watch. Onstage, eight scenes from “Viewing the Lanterns,” an episode in The Eight Loyalists, were being performed. At the height of the merriment, Baoyu left his seat and headed outside. Grandmother Jia called, “Where are you going? The firecrackers outside are fierce. Take care that burning paper does not fall from the sky and set you alight.” Baoyu replied, “I am not going far. I shall only step outside and come straight back.” Grandmother Jia ordered the old serving-women to follow him carefully. Thus Baoyu went out, accompanied only by Sheyue, Qiuwen, and several young maids. Grandmother Jia then asked, “Why is Xiren nowhere to be seen? She is becoming rather self-important these days, sending only the little girls out to attend him.” Lady Wang hurriedly rose and explained with a smile, “Her mother died the other day. Since she is in fresh mourning, it would not be proper for her to appear here in front.” Grandmother Jia nodded, then said with a smile, “When one is attending one's master, there can be no question of observing mourning or not. If she still attended me, do you suppose she would not be here now? It is all because we have been too indulgent. With plenty of servants at hand, we pay no attention to such things, and now it has become customary.” Xifeng hurried over and replied with a smile, “Even if she were not in mourning tonight, someone would still have to watch the Garden. Lamps, candles, and fireworks are especially hazardous. With an opera being performed here, who in the Garden would not steal over for a look? She is attentive and can make the rounds to see that all is well. Besides, when this gathering ends and Brother Bao goes back to bed, everything will be ready for him. If she came here too, the others would grow careless. When we dispersed and he returned, his bedding would be cold, the tea and water would not be ready, and everything would be inconvenient. That is why I told her not to come but simply to watch the rooms. When we disperse, all will be in readiness; we need not worry here, and she can also fulfill the proprieties of mourning. Does that not benefit all three sides? If Ancestress wishes to summon her, I shall have her brought here at once.” Hearing this, Grandmother Jia hastily said, “What you say is quite right and more thoughtful than anything I had considered. By all means, do not summon her. But when did her mother die? How is it that I knew nothing of it?” Xifeng said with a smile, “Xiren came and reported it to you herself the other day. How could you have forgotten?” Grandmother Jia thought for a moment and said with a smile, “Now I remember. My memory really is not what it used to be.” Everyone laughed and said, “How could you be expected to remember such things, Old Madam?” Grandmother Jia sighed again. “I was thinking how she attended me for a time from childhood, and then attended Yun'er for a time, until at last she was given to that little demon Baoyu. Heaven knows how he has plagued her these past few years. Nor is she a bondservant born and bred in our household, and she has never received any very great favor from us. When her mother died, I meant to give her a few taels of silver for the funeral, but I forgot all about it.” Xifeng said, “The other day, Madam gave her forty taels of silver. That should suffice.”

p.src: Meanwhile, Baoyu went straight into the Garden. Seeing that he was returning to his rooms, the old serving-women did not follow but sat warming themselves in the gatehouse tearoom, stealing the opportunity to drink and play cards with the women in charge of the tea. When Baoyu reached the courtyard, the lamps shone brilliantly, yet not a voice could be heard. Sheyue said, “Can they all be asleep? Let us slip in quietly and give them a fright.” They all crept in on tiptoe and peered past the mirrored screen. Xiren and one or two others were reclining opposite each other on the heated platform, while two or three old nurses dozed at the far end. Baoyu assumed that the two women were asleep and was just about to enter when he suddenly heard Yuanyang sigh and say, “It only shows how uncertain everything in this world is. By rights, with you living here alone and your parents away, wandering east and west each year with no fixed abode, one would have thought you could never be present at their deathbeds. Yet as fate would have it, your mother died here this year, and you were able to go out and see her through her last moments.” “Exactly,” said Xiren. I never imagined I would be able to see either of my parents through to the end. Madam also gave me forty taels of silver. That more than repays me for having been raised here, and I dare ask for nothing further.” On hearing this, Baoyu hastily turned and whispered to Sheyue and the others, “Who would have thought she had come here too? If I go in, she will take offense and leave again. We had better go back and let the two of them talk quietly for a while. Xiren was grieving here all alone; fortunately, Yuanyang came at just the right time.” So saying, he quietly withdrew again.

p.src: Baoyu went behind a rock, stood there, and lifted his robe. Sheyue and Qiuwen stopped and turned their backs, laughing as they said, “Squat down before you undo your underclothes, or the wind may chill your stomach.” The two little maids behind them, realizing that he was relieving himself, hurried ahead to the tea room to make preparations. Just as Baoyu came back around, two married servants approached from the opposite direction and called out to ask who was there. Qiuwen said, “Baoyu is here. If you keep shouting like that, mind you do not startle him.” The women hastily laughed and said, “We did not know. What a calamity to bring upon ourselves during the great festival! You young ladies must have been working very hard these past few days.” As they spoke, they had already drawn near. Sheyue and the others asked, “What are you carrying?” The women replied, “These are delicacies the Old Lady awarded to Miss Jin and Miss Hua.” Qiuwen laughed. “They are performing The Eight Righteous Men outside, not The Primordial Box. So where has this ‘Goddess of Golden Flowers’ sprung from?” Baoyu said with a smile, “Open them and let me see.” Qiuwen and Sheyue hurried forward and opened the two boxes. The two women quickly crouched down. Baoyu saw that both boxes contained the finest fruits and dishes from the banquet. He nodded and walked on. Sheyue and Qiuwen hastily tossed the lids back on and caught up with him. Baoyu smiled and said, “Those two women are pleasant and know how to speak. They toil every day, yet they said that you have been working hard these past few days. At least they are not the sort who boast of their own merits.” Sheyue said, “The good ones are very good indeed, but the ill-mannered ones are altogether too ill-mannered.” Baoyu smiled. “You are sensible girls. Simply make allowances for them as poor, clumsy people, and let that be the end of it.” Talking all the while, they reached the garden gate. Though the old serving women there had been drinking and playing cards, they had kept coming out to see what was happening. When they saw Baoyu arrive, they all followed along. When they reached the rear veranda of the flower hall, they found the two little maids waiting there. One held a small washbasin, while the other carried a towel and a little flask of scented lotion. Qiuwen quickly put her hand into the basin to test the water and said, “The older you get, the more careless you become. Where did you get water this cold?” The little maid laughed. “Just consider the weather, miss! I was afraid the water would be cold, so I went out of my way to pour in boiling water, and even that has grown cold.” As they were speaking, an old serving woman happened to approach carrying a kettle of boiling water. The little maid called, “Be a dear, granny, and come pour some in for me.” The old woman said, “My dear girl, this water is for the Old Lady’s tea. You had better go and ladle some out yourself; it is hardly far to walk.” Qiuwen said, “No matter whose water it is, will you refuse us? I will simply empty the Old Lady’s own teakettle and use that water to wash our hands.”

Let them have some piping-hot soup and dishes before they sing again.” She also ordered that some of the assorted fruits, rice dumplings, and other foods be taken to them. Once the performance had stopped, an old serving woman brought in two female storytellers who regularly visited the household. Two stools were set for them at one side, and a three-stringed lute and a pipa were handed to them. Grandmother Jia asked Li and Xue what story they wished to hear. Both replied, “Anything will do.” Grandmother Jia then asked, “Have you added any new stories lately?” The two storytellers replied, “There is a new tale set in the waning Tang and Five Dynasties period.” Asked its title, one of the women said, “It is called The Phoenix Seeks the Luan.” “That is a fine title,” said Grandmother Jia. “I wonder how it came by that name. First tell us the story in outline, and if it sounds good, you may perform it.” The storyteller began, “The tale says that during the waning years of the Tang there lived a country gentleman, a native of Jinling, named Wang Zhong, who had served as chief minister under two emperors. He has now retired and returned home, and his only child is a son named Wang Xifeng.” At this, everyone burst out laughing. Grandmother Jia laughed. “He has the very same name as our Feng.” A serving woman hurried over and nudged the storyteller. “That is Second Mistress's name. Do not talk such nonsense.” “Go on, go on,” said Grandmother Jia with a laugh. The storyteller hastily rose with an embarrassed smile. “We deserve to die! We did not know it was Mistress's revered name.” Xifeng laughed. “What is there to fear? Just carry on. Plenty of people share both their family and given names.” The storyteller resumed. “That year, Master Wang sent young Master Wang to the capital to sit the examinations. One day he was caught in a heavy downpour and entered a country estate to take shelter. As it happened, the owner of the estate was another country gentleman, surnamed Li, whose family had been friends with Master Wang's for generations. He therefore invited the young gentleman to stay in his study. This gentleman Li had no sons, but only one cherished daughter. Her fragrant name was Chuluan, and she was accomplished in the qin, chess, calligraphy, and painting.” Grandmother Jia hastily interrupted, “No wonder it is called The Phoenix Seeks the Luan. They portray other people's daughters as utterly depraved, yet still call them beauties. Their inventions bear not the faintest resemblance to reality.

p.src: They invariably begin with a distinguished scholarly family, in which the father is either a minister or a chief minister, and any daughter born to him is sure to be treasured like a jewel. This young lady is inevitably learned, well-mannered, and accomplished in everything—a peerless beauty. Yet the moment she sees one handsome young man, whether a kinsman or a family friend, she starts contemplating marriage. She forgets her parents and all the precepts she has read, and behaves neither like an honest soul nor even a proper thief. What part of that makes her a beauty? However full of learning she may be, once she behaves in such a fashion she can no longer be counted a beauty. Suppose a man steeped in learning becomes a thief. Would the law call him a gifted scholar and refuse to charge him with theft? Plainly, the authors of such books contradict themselves. Besides, if these are truly young ladies from great families of hereditary officials and scholars, educated in books and propriety, with mothers who are themselves learned and well-mannered, then even if the fathers have retired home, such grand households must naturally contain many people, including numerous nurses and maids to attend the young ladies. Why, then, whenever such things happen in these stories, are there only the young lady and one maid constantly at her side? Just think: what are all those other people supposed to be doing? Does that not show that the beginning and end of the story fail to agree?” Everyone laughed on hearing this. “With the old lady's explanation, every one of their lies has been exposed.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “There is a reason for it. Some who write such books envy other families' wealth and rank, or have failed to obtain some favor they sought, and so invent stories to besmirch them. Others have read so many of these books that they have become bewitched by them. They too long for a beauty of their own, and so write such stories to amuse themselves. p.src: Xifeng came forward to pour the wine and said with a laugh, “Enough, enough! The wine is getting cold. Have a sip to moisten your throat, Old Ancestress, before you go on exposing those lies. This episode shall be called ‘The Tale of Exposing Lies,’ and it takes place in this very dynasty, in this very place, in this very year, month, day, and hour. Since even the Old Ancestress cannot tell two stories at once, when two blossoms open we must describe each branch in turn. So, leaving aside for now whether it is truth or falsehood, let us first deal with those watching the lanterns and the plays. Old Ancestress, why not let these two relatives drink a cup and watch a couple of plays, and then begin untangling yesterday’s story?” She laughed and talked as she poured the wine, and before she had finished, everyone was doubled over with laughter. The two female storytellers could not stop laughing either. “What a ready tongue you have, madam! If you took up storytelling, you would truly leave us no way to earn our bread.” Aunt Xue laughed. “Do curb your high spirits a little. There are people outside; things are not as they usually are.” Xifeng laughed. “The only person outside is Cousin Zhen. We still regard each other as brother and sister, and we have been getting into mischief together since childhood. Only since we became related by marriage these past few years have I begun observing so many formalities. And even if we had not been brother and sister from childhood, but reckoned our relation by the senior and junior branches of the family, there is still the story in The Twenty-four Exemplars of Filial Piety about ‘wearing motley robes to amuse one’s parents.’ Since they cannot come and perform to make the Old Ancestress laugh, while I have managed with some difficulty to make her laugh and eat a little more, everyone ought to be pleased and thank me. Surely they would not laugh at me instead?” Grandmother Jia laughed. “Indeed, for the last two days I have not had one really hearty laugh. It is thanks to her that I have laughed all this while and feel somewhat lighter at heart. I shall have another cup of wine.” As she drank, she instructed Baoyu, “You too must offer your elder sister a cup.” Xifeng laughed. “There is no need for him to offer me one. I shall beg longevity from the Old Ancestress instead.” With that, she picked up Grandmother Jia’s cup, drank the half cup of wine remaining in it, handed it to a maid, and had it replaced with another cup that had been soaking in warm water. The cups at every table were then removed, and fresh wine was poured into the replacement cups kept warm in water and brought in, after which Xifeng returned to her seat.

p.src: One of the female storytellers said, “If the Old Ancestress does not care to hear this story, perhaps we might play a piece for you instead.” Grandmother Jia said, “Then the two of you play ‘The General’s Command’ together.” At this, the two women hurriedly tuned their strings, set the mode, and began to play. Grandmother Jia then asked, “What watch of the night is it?” The old serving-women hastily replied, “It is the third watch.” “No wonder it is beginning to feel so chilly,” said Grandmother Jia. The maids had already brought additional and warmer clothes for everyone to put on. Lady Wang rose and said with a smile, “Why not move into the warm chamber, Old Madam, and sit on the heated platform? These two relatives are no strangers, and the rest of us can keep you company.” Grandmother Jia heard her out and laughed. “If that is what you think, why should we not all move inside? Would that not be warmer?” “I fear there may not be room for everyone inside,” said Lady Wang. Grandmother Jia laughed. “I have a way. We need not use all these tables now. Just put two or three together, and we can all sit close beside one another. It will be both intimate and warm.” Everyone agreed, “That will be great fun.” So saying, they rose from the banquet. The married servants hurriedly cleared away what remained of the feast. Inside, they joined three large tables end to end and set out fresh fruit and dishes. Grandmother Jia said, “Let us dispense with all ceremony. It will be best if you simply sit where I tell you.” She seated Aunt Xue and Li Wan’s mother in the places of honor facing the room, while she herself sat facing west. She called Baoqin, Daiyu, and Xiangyun to sit close on either side of her, and said to Baoyu, “You sit beside your mother.” Thus Baoyu sat between Lady Xing and Lady Wang. Baochai and the other young ladies sat along the western side; after them, in order, came Madam Lou with Jia Jun, then You-shi and Li Wan with Jia Lan between them, while Jia Rong’s wife sat crosswise at the lower end. Grandmother Jia then said, “Zhen, take your brothers and go. I shall soon be going to bed myself.”

p.src: Presently, the instructor from Pear Fragrance Court led Wen’guan and the other twelve players out through a side gate off the covered walk. Several old women carried a few soft bundles. As there had been no time to bring the trunks, they had selected and brought the costumes for three or five pieces they thought Grandmother Jia would enjoy. The old women brought Wen’guan and the others in to pay their respects, after which the girls stood silently with their hands lowered. Grandmother Jia laughed. “Even during the New Year festivities, your teacher will not let you go out and enjoy yourselves. What will you perform? Those eight scenes from The Eight Righteous Ones just now were so noisy they gave me a headache. Let us have something more subdued. Just look: Aunt Xue and our relative Madam Li both come from households with their own theatrical troupes; who knows how many fine performances they have heard? These young ladies too have seen finer plays and heard finer songs than the young ladies of our household. And now these young players belong to the troupe of that celebrated connoisseur of the theatre. Children though they are, they are even better than a full adult company. We must not give anyone cause to criticize us; we shall have to devise something novel. Have Fang’guan perform ‘Seeking the Dream,’ accompanied only by the fiddle together with the pipes and xiao; do not use the mouth organ or flute at all.” Wen’guan laughed. “Quite right. Naturally, our performances could never meet the standards of the aunts, the related ladies, and the young ladies. You need only listen to one of us enunciate her lines and another display her voice.” “Precisely,” Grandmother Jia replied with a laugh. Aunt Li and Aunt Xue laughed delightedly. “What a quick-witted child! She has joined the Old Lady in teasing us.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “Ours is merely an amusement arranged however we please, not a company that goes out to earn money, so naturally it is not much in keeping with current fashion.” Then she added, “Have Kui’guan perform ‘Huiming Delivers the Letter,’ without painting her face. We shall use just these two pieces to let them hear something unusual. But if you spare the least effort, I shall not forgive you.” On hearing this, Wen’guan and the others withdrew and hurried to put on their costumes and take the stage. First came ‘Seeking the Dream,’ followed by ‘Delivering the Letter.’ Everyone listened in utter silence. Aunt Xue then laughed and said, “They truly deserve praise. I have watched hundreds of companies, yet never have I seen one accompanied by xiao and pipes.” “It is done,” said Grandmother Jia. “Only, in a song such as ‘The Chu River under a Clear Sky’ from West Tower, a young male-role actor will often play the xiao as accompaniment. It is indeed rare for an entire suite like this; that merely depends on whether the master of the household cares to be particular about such things. What is so extraordinary about it?” Pointing at Xiangyun, she continued, “When I was her age, her grandfather kept a troupe of young players. It happened that an accomplished qin player joined them, so in such pieces as ‘Listening to the Qin’ from The Western Chamber, ‘Flirtation by Qin’ from The Jade Hairpin, and ‘The Eighteen Songs of a Nomad Flute’ from The Sequel to the Lute, the music became completely authentic. How would you compare that with this?” “That was rarer still,” everyone agreed.

p.src: At that point, Jia Rong and his wife presented wine to the company. Seeing Grandmother Jia in exceptionally high spirits, Xifeng laughed and said, “Since the lady storytellers are here, why not have them beat the drum while we pass a spray of plum blossom and play a round of ‘Spring Joy Reaches the Brows’?” Grandmother Jia laughed. “That is an excellent game, perfectly suited to the season and the occasion.” She promptly ordered someone to fetch a black-lacquered, copper-studded ornamental game drum for the lady storytellers to beat, while a branch of red plum blossom was taken from the banquet table. Grandmother Jia laughed. “When the drum stops, whoever is holding it must drink a cup—but ought she not also have to say something?” Xifeng laughed. “In my opinion, who but our Old Ancestress possesses every accomplishment one could ask for? For those of us who lack such talents, would that not spoil the fun? I think the forfeit should appeal to refined and common tastes alike: whoever loses must tell a joke.” Everyone knew that she was habitually adept at telling jokes and had an inexhaustible store of fresh and amusing tales. Her proposal delighted not only everyone at the banquet but also all the servants, old and young, waiting upon them below. The little maids all hurried out, seeking out their older and younger companions to tell them, “Come quickly and listen! Second Mistress is telling jokes again.” Soon the maids had crowded the room. The plays and music were then brought to an end. Grandmother Jia ordered soup, pastries, fruit, and vegetables to be given to Wen’guan and the others, then commanded the drumming to begin. The lady storytellers were all practiced hands. Now fast, now slow, their drumming sounded at times like drops from a water clock near dawn, at times like beans bursting from a pan, at times like startled horses galloping wildly, and at times like a flash of lightning suddenly swallowed by darkness. When the drumbeat slowed, the plum branch passed slowly; when the drumbeat quickened, the branch passed quickly. Just as the branch reached Grandmother Jia’s hands, the drumming abruptly stopped. Everyone burst out laughing, and Jia Rong hurried forward to pour her a cup of wine. “Naturally the Old Lady must receive the first good fortune,” everyone said with a laugh. “Only then may some of that good fortune fall to us.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “Drinking the wine is easy enough, but telling the joke is rather difficult.” Everyone said, “Your jokes are better and more numerous even than Xifeng’s. Please favor us with one so that we may have a laugh.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “I have nothing new or especially amusing. Still, I must brazen it out and tell you one.” She began, “There was once a family with ten sons, each of whom took a wife. Only the tenth daughter-in-law was clever, quick-witted, and sweet-tongued. Her parents-in-law doted on her and complained all day long that the other nine were unfilial. The other nine daughters-in-law felt deeply wronged and discussed the matter among themselves: ‘All nine of us are truly filial at heart, but none of us is as sweet-tongued as that little hussy. So now that our parents-in-law are old, they praise only her. To whom can we appeal against such an injustice?’

p.src: The eldest daughter-in-law had an idea and said, ‘Tomorrow, let us go and burn incense at the Temple of the King of Hell. We shall ask His Infernal Majesty why, when he sent us to be born as human beings, he gave that little hussy alone such a clever tongue and made all the rest of us dull-witted.’ They were all delighted and agreed that it was an excellent idea. p.src: On hearing this, Jia Rong hurried outside and directed the young servants to set up screens in the courtyard and arrange and hang all the fireworks in readiness. These fireworks were all tribute gifts from various regions. Though not especially large, they were exquisitely ingenious, depicting stories of every kind and interspersed with multicolored firecrackers. Lin Daiyu was delicate by nature and could not bear the crackling reports, so Grandmother Jia gathered her into her arms. Aunt Xue put her arms around Xiangyun. “I'm not afraid,” Xiangyun said with a laugh. Baochai and the others laughed. “She especially loves setting off great firecrackers herself. How could this frighten her?” Lady Wang then drew Baoyu into her arms. “So there is no one to cherish us,” Xifeng said with a laugh. “You have me,” said Madam You, laughing. “I'll hold you. Aren't you ashamed? There you go acting like a spoiled child again. The moment you hear firecrackers, it's as though you've eaten honeybee droppings—you've grown giddy again today!” Xifeng laughed. “When everyone has gone, let's set some off in our garden. I can set them off better than the young servants can.” As they spoke, one kind after another was repeatedly set off outside, along with many smaller fireworks called Stars Filling the Sky, Nine Dragons Entering the Clouds, A Single Thunderclap, and Ten Bursts in Flight. When the fireworks were over, the young performers were ordered to give a rendition of “Lotus-Fall.” Coins were scattered all over the stage, and the children were told to scramble after them for everyone's amusement. When soup was served again, Grandmother Jia said, “The night is long, and I am beginning to feel a little hungry.” Xifeng promptly replied, “We have duck-meat congee ready.” “I would rather have something light,” said Grandmother Jia. Xifeng hastened to say, “There is also polished-rice congee simmered with dates, prepared for the ladies observing a meatless diet.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “Everything is either greasy or sweet.” Xifeng quickly added, “There is almond cream as well, though I fear that is sweet too.” “That will do well enough,” said Grandmother Jia. As she spoke, she ordered the remains of the banquet cleared away, and a fresh array of exquisite little dishes was laid outside. Everyone ate a little of whatever they fancied, took the tea served for rinsing their mouths, and only then dispersed.

p.src: Early on the seventeenth, they went over to the Ning mansion once more to perform the rites; after attending the closing of the ancestral shrine and putting away the ancestral portraits, they returned home. That day, it was Aunt Xue's household that invited them to a New Year feast. Grandmother Jia attended some of these households and not others.
